item.title: Some complete $\omega$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.16473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $\Sigma^\omega$ in $\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k$, and by $\checked{D}_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $\Sigma$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $\omega$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\in\Sigma^\omega\mid\forall i\in\omega ~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $\checked{D}\_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0\_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k>3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbf{\Delta}^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].
item.dc:creator: Jacques Duparc (UNIL), Olivier Finkel (IMJ-PRG), Dominique Lecomte (IMJ-PRG)

item.title: On the Complexity of Level-Synchronized Tree Automata for Quantum Circuit Verification
item.description: arXiv:2610.25138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable quantum computation requires methods for verifying quantum circuits. Level-synchronized tree automata (LSTAs) were recently introduced to represent sets of quantum states for this purpose. We study LSTAs along two axes relevant to verification: the complexity of their decision problems and the size of their representations under circuit operations. We prove that acyclic LSTAs have NP-complete nonemptiness and $\Pi_2^P$-complete language inclusion, and that general language inclusion is EXPSPACE-complete. We further prove inherent quadratic representation growth under individual quantum gates in a fixed qubit order, and give an adjacent-qubit reordering construction that preserves level synchronization. These results clarify the scope of applicability of the automata-theoretic toolbox for quantum circuit verification.
item.dc:creator: Michael Blondin, Samy Chady Khoumsi-Kasmi, Guillermo A. P\'erez, Marnix Suilen

item.title: Reward Objectives for Robust (PO)MDPs: A Law-Preserving Equivalence with (Partially Observable) Games
item.description: arXiv:2610.26568v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robust partially observable Markov decision processes model agents that act under partial observability while adversarial environment resolves uncertainty in the transition probabilities. Reward objectives such as discounted-sum, long-run average and cumulative reward under finite and infinite horizons allow quantifying the utility of an agent. We consider the problem of solving RPOMDPs under all four reward objectives, where the goal is to decide whether the value of a risk measure with respect to a reward objective exceeds a given threshold. We consider different risk measures, such as (1)~expected value, (2)~mean-variance (MV), (3)~conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), and (4)~entropic risk (ERisk). Our results can be summarized as follows. First, we formalize the class of law-invariant risk measures, that subsume all four risk measures above. Second, we propose a unified framework for solving RPOMDPs with discounted-sum, long-run average and cumulative reward objectives under any law-invariant risk measure, by reducing the problem to solving partially observable stochastic games (POSGs). Our unified framework applies to (s,a)-rectangular RPOMDPs with polytopic uncertainty sets, which we show to be {\em equivalent} to POSGs, for each of the four reward objectives and any law-invariant risk measure. We prove equivalence by designing logspace reductions between the RPOMDP and POSG models, that map strategies to strategies and preserve the distribution of the reward objective, up to a constant rescaling factor. Third, as a corollary, we derive new computational complexity results for R(PO)MDPs and POSGs. In particular, we show that solving (s,a)-rectangular RMDPs is as hard as solving simple stochastic games.
item.dc:creator: Durgam Latha, Dion Reji, Dorde Zikelic, Shankaranarayanan Krishna

item.title: Evaluating Massively Parallel Algorithms for DFA Minimisation, Equivalence Checking and Inclusion Checking
item.description: arXiv:2508.20735v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study parallel algorithms for the minimisation and equivalence checking of Deterministic Finite Automata (DFAs). Regarding DFA minimisation, we implement four different massively parallel algorithms on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). Our results confirm the expectations that the algorithm with the theoretically best time complexity is not practically suitable to run on GPUs due to the large amount of resources needed. We empirically verify that parallel partition refinement algorithms from the literature perform better in practice, even though their time complexity is worse. Furthermore, we introduce a novel algorithm based on partition refinement with an extra parallel partial transitive closure step and show that on specific benchmarks it has better run-time complexity and performs better in practice. In addition, we address checking the language equivalence and inclusion of two DFAs. We consider the Hopcroft-Karp algorithm, and explain how a variant of it can be parallelised for GPUs. We note that these problems can be encoded for the GPU-accelerated model checker GPUexplore, allowing the use its lockless hash table and fine-grained parallel work distribution mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Jan Heemstra, Jan Martens, Anton Wijs

item.title: Symmetric two-counter machines
item.description: arXiv:2610.23495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Counter machines are a particularly simple, Turing-complete model of computation. We study the expressive power of nondeterministic 2-counter machines which are symmetric, in that their set of update transitions is invariant under swapping of counters. Our model is an extension of symmetric 2-VASS, in that we allow modifying both counters within a single transition. As the main result we demonstrate a dramatic impact of symmetry: we show that symmetric 2-counter machines are not Turing-complete, by proving decidability of their reachability problem. We conjecture that the decidability extends to machines with 3 or more counters that are symmetric, meaning the set of update transitions is invariant under any permutation of counters. We leave this problem open for machines with 3 and more counters, while identifying a frontier of the impact of symmetry: we prove undecidability for 3-counter machines invariant under the cyclic permutation group of order 3.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Jaros, {\L}ukasz Kami\'nski, Maja K\k{a}dzio{\l}ka, S{\l}awomir Lasota

item.title: A Dichotomy Theorem for Homomorphism Problems on Automatic Structures
item.description: arXiv:2602.18238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The field of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) studies homomorphism problems between relational structures where the target structure is fixed. Classifying the complexity of these problems has been a central quest of the field, notably when both sides are finite structures. In this paper, we study the generalization where the input is an automatic structure---potentially infinite, but describable by finite automata. We prove a striking dichotomy: homomorphism problems over automatic structures are either decidable in non-deterministic logarithmic space (NL), or undecidable. We show that structures for which the problem is decidable are exactly those with finite duality, which is a classical property of target structures asserting that the existence of a homomorphism into them can be characterized by the absence of a finite set of obstructions in the source structure. Notably, this property precisely characterizes target structures whose homomorphism problem is definable in first-order logic, which is well-known to be decidable over automatic structures. We also consider a natural variant of the problem. While automatic structures are finitely describable, homomorphisms from them into finite structures need not be. This leads to the notion of "regular homomorphism", where the homomorphism itself must be describable by finite automata. Remarkably, we prove that this variant exhibits the same dichotomy, with the same characterization for decidability.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Cuvelier, R\'emi Morvan

item.title: At the Limits of Computability: Steps Towards Autonomous AI Discovery on the Busy Beaver Frontier
item.description: arXiv:2610.22603v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in AI for mathematics---ranging from Olympiad medal performances to resolving long-standing open conjectures---have rapidly expanded what automated systems can achieve. Yet these successes primarily concern predefined, human-formulated problems, leaving open how AI systems can autonomously uncover mathematical structure and formulate new questions. To push beyond static challenges, we explore the Busy Beaver (BB) domain, an uncomputable frontier that is fundamentally open-ended. Because no algorithm can compute the Busy Beaver number $\mathrm{BB}(n)$ for every $n$, this domain provides a natural setting for sustained exploration through mathematical conjecture and proof. In this paper, we introduce a Gemini-based agentic pipeline that automatically discovers accelerations of Turing machines, expressed as compact mathematical rules summarizing many execution steps. Our system integrates pattern recognition, automated conjecturing, informal mathematical reasoning, and formal theorem proving in Lean. With this framework, our system autonomously discovered and formally verified novel Collatz-like accelerations for eleven machines in $\mathrm{BB}(6)$. Subject to community acceptance, we provisionally classify these machines as Cryptids, namely machines whose blank-tape executions admit exact, compact mathematical descriptions but whose halting behavior remains unresolved. These results advance the analysis of $\mathrm{BB}(6)$ holdouts on the Busy Beaver frontier and demonstrate the potential of autonomous AI systems for open-ended mathematical discovery in fundamental computer science.
item.dc:creator: Marco Dos Santos, Vivek Veeriah, Alex Havrilla, Andrew Bolt, Goran Zuzic, Satinder Singh, Tom Zahavy
